parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.lead:
Fig. 5.1 shows two parallel conducting plates that are in a vacuum. The plates are separated by a distance of 6.7 cm and have a potential difference (p.d.) of 430 V between them.

[[fig:f1]]
parts.text: On Fig. 5.1, draw four field lines to represent the electric field between the plates.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Determine the strength *E* of the electric field between the plates.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text:
An electron travels at a speed of 2.6 × 10⁷ m s⁻¹ towards the region between the plates, as shown in Fig. 5.1.

On Fig. 5.1, draw the path of the electron as it moves between and beyond the plates.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.lead: A uniform magnetic field is now applied in the region of the electric field in Fig. 5.1, so that the electron in (b)(iii) travels undeviated through the region.
parts.text: Determine the direction of the uniform magnetic field.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Explain, with reference to the forces exerted by the two fields on the electron, why the path of the electron is undeviated.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text: Determine the flux density *B* of the uniform magnetic field. Give a unit with your answer.

figures.caption: Fig. 5.1
figures.alt: Two horizontal conducting plates are shown with a +430 V connection to the upper plate, a 0 V connection to the lower plate, and a 6.7 cm separation; an electron moves horizontally toward the region between them.
